item.title: NH Education Trends in Southern NH — October 16, 2026: The Southern NH Squeeze
item.description:
Alex and Jordan open the new weekly show with the trend pressing on every southern New Hampshire district at once: falling enrollment, universal school choice, and dropping state aid arriving together — and what district leaders can do about it.
Sources — NH Fiscal Policy Institute (Oct 2026), educator workforce report: https://nhfpi.org/resource/new-hampshires-educator-workforce-faces-growing-recruitment-retirement-and-affordability-pressures/ ; Keene Sentinel / Granite State News Collaborative (Aug 2026), EFA cap: https://www.keenesentinel.com/state_news/nh-s-school-voucher-program-expands-to-12-500-students-hundreds-on-wait-list/article_99646690-eb07-4c2c-bf0a-02cfb451d404.html ; Nashua Ink Link (Oct 2026), facilities plan: https://nashua.inklink.news/nashua-school-board-sets-oct-21-presentation-nov-16-vote-on-facilities-plan/ ; Manchester Ink Link (Oct 2026), class sizes and staffing: https://manchester.inklink.news/manchester-schools-see-some-class-size-improvement-but-staffing-pressures-remain/ ; NHED (Sept 2, 2026), 2026 assessment results: https://www.education.nh.gov/news-and-media/nhed-announces-2026-student-assessment-results ; Business NH Magazine, Children's Scholarship Fund NH on EFA demand: https://www.businessnhmagazine.com/article/nhrsquos-school-choice-program-hits-enrollment-cap-and-has-300-students-on-a-waitlist ; NHED charter school funding documents (FY25–FY27): https://gc.nh.gov/lba/budget/operating_budgets/2026-2027/HF_Division_II/Division II - NHED Charter School Funding Documents - 03-10-25.pdf ; Londonderry sample ballot (per-pupil and proficiency figures): https://www.londonderrynh.gov/DocumentCenter/View/2396/Sample-School-Ballot-PDF?bidId= ; PublicSchoolReview, Manchester charter schools: https://www.publicschoolreview.com/new-hampshire/manchester/charter ; Nashua Ink Link (Oct 2026), library workers rally: https://nashua.inklink.news/nashua-public-library-employees-going-on-100-days-without-new-contract-as-supporters-rally/ . To verify the WMUR Nashua M shortfall report, search WMUR for Nashua school system facing dollar 2M shortfall after state aid drops (Oct 14, 2026). To verify CNHI's EFA demographic figures, search cnhinews for EFA double percentage low-income recipients Rindge 28.7. To verify teacher salary rankings, search World Population Review average teacher salary by state 2026. Long-view enrollment figures are October 1 census data via the nhschooldata project, sourced from the NH DOE iPlatform: search nhschooldata enrollment trends.

item.title: [NH] NH Education Trends in Southern NH — October 23, 2026: HB 1817 and the Free Seat
item.description:
Alex and Jordan devote the full hour to House Bill 1817, the 2026 law giving resident Education Freedom Account students free seats in their district classes, clubs, teams, and career and technical programs while the state sends districts no funding for those seats, and trace what that means for Manchester, Nashua, Derry, Salem, and the southern New Hampshire corridor in its first fall.
Sources: - HB 1817 as adopted by both bodies, with fiscal note (NH Department of Education: likely significant cost at local, state, or both level; impact indeterminable; about $6,000 per career and technical seat): https://gc.nh.gov/bill_status/pdf.aspx?id=32821&q=billVersion - HB 1817 legislative history and votes (House 179-156, Senate 15-8, signed June 19, 2026, Chapter 183, effective August 18, 2026): https://legiscan.com/NH/bill/HB1817/2026 - NH Department of Education, Technical Assistance Advisory on HB 1817 (issued September 25, 2026; districts asked to review enrollment and fee policies): https://www.education.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt326/files/inline-documents/2026/ta-hb1817.pdf - NH Department of Education, Technical Advisory on access to public school curricular and cocurricular programs, RSA 193:1-c (home educated students in grades 7-12 counted in average daily membership for adequacy aid): http://doe.nhdoit.acsitefactory.com/sites/g/files/ehbemt326/files/inline-documents/sonh/technical-advisory-rsa193-1-c.pdf - Reaching Higher NH, Recapping the 2026 Legislative Session (HB 1817 summary, 50 percent enrollment cap, district cost warning): https://www.reachinghighernh.org/content-item/554/2026-legislative-recap - New Hampshire School Boards Association, 2026 Legislative Summary (resident-only scope, instructional time measurement unresolved): https://nhsba.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/FINAL-2026-NHSBA-LEG-SUMMARY-8.18.2026.pdf - NEA-NH, New Education Laws guide (HB 1817 access without the state support given for home education students): https://neanh.org/advocating-change/new-from-nea-nh/090526-nea-nh-legislative-update-new-education-laws-state-primary - Childrens Scholarship Fund New Hampshire, EFA program reaches 12,500-student enrollment cap for 2026-27 (13,443 eligible, 943 waitlisted): https://nh.scholarshipfund.org/new-hampshire-education-freedom-account-program-reaches-12500-student-enrollment-cap/ - RSA 194-F:2, Education Freedom Account program and qualifying expenses, including services contracted from a district public school: https://law.justia.com/codes/new-hampshire/title-xv/chapter-194-f/section-194-f-2/ - EdChoice, New Hampshire Education Freedom Account program stats (average account value about $4,795 in 2025-26, cap escalator): https://www.edchoice.org/school-choice/programs/education-freedom-account-program/ - NH Education Department Special Education Procedural Safeguards Handbook, December 2024 (parentally placed students, equitable services, services plans): https://files.smartsites.parentsquare.com/8931/nhed_special_education_procedural_safeguards_handbook_-_updated_december_2024.pdf - NH Career and Technical Education, Parents page (28 centers statewide; a two-year CTE program costs about $8,000 more than standard tuition): https://nh-cte.org/parents/ - NH School Scoop, October 13, 2026 (Manchester class size caps of 20, 25, and 24 for labs; HB 1817 summary): https://nhschoolscoop.substack.com/p/nh-school-scoop-october-13-2026
To verify items without a stable URL: (1) New Hampshire Bulletin, October 12, 2026 reporting on the September 25 advisory and district capacity, prerequisite, and tryout limits: search newhampshirebulletin.com for HB 1817 EFA public school classes October 2026. (2) Town and county EFA take-up rates (Manchester about 9 percent; Rockingham County 10 percent rising to 15 percent): search the New Hampshire Bulletin for education freedom accounts double low-income recipients, which reports the Department of Education town-level data. (3) Timberlane Regional High School CTE budget figures (about $270,000 tuition, about $156,289 transportation, 143 to 158 students) and the Londonderry CTE consultant figures (about 149 students, $2,000 to $3,000 per student): search citizenportal.ai for Timberlane Regional High School CTE budget and for Londonderry School District CTE consultant.

item.title: [NH] NH Education Trends in Southern NH — October 30, 2026: The Empty Seat
item.description:
Chronic absenteeism is the trend underneath every other trend in southern New Hampshire: how New Hampshire counts the students who miss ten percent or more of the year, how the state rate climbed from about thirteen percent before the pandemic to nearly thirty four percent at the peak, what Manchester, Salem, and Londonderry are each doing about it in the fall of twenty twenty six, and what the newest national research says actually works.
Sources: - Manchester Ink Link, January 24, 2026 — Manchester's 2024-25 chronic absenteeism data (just over 30% district-wide; high schools 37%, middle schools 27%, elementary 21%), the 25% goal, and the "movable middle" strategy: https://manchester.inklink.news/officials-say-movable-middle-provides-key-to-chronically-absent-third-of-manchester-students/ - Manchester Ink Link, October 22, 2026 — Board of Mayor and Aldermen approves the Office of Youth Services pilot (January 2027 through June 2028) with the Manchester School District: https://manchester.inklink.news/bma-approves-mayor-ruais-proposal-to-enhance-office-of-youth-services-role/ - U.S. Department of Education, ED Data Express — New Hampshire chronically absent students: 33.9% in 2021-22 (55,972 of 164,951) and 24.8% in 2022-23 (40,488 of 163,303). Verify: go to eddataexpress.ed.gov, Data Download Tool, select state New Hampshire, data group "Percent students chronically absent" (814PCT), population Chronically Absent Students. - Education Recovery Scorecard (Harvard CEPR / Stanford) — New Hampshire chronic absenteeism about 13% in 2019 and about 24% in 2023; math about half a grade level and reading more than a third of a grade level below 2019. Verify: educationrecoveryscorecard.org, States, New Hampshire. - American Enterprise Institute, Return to Learn Tracker — Nat Malkus, "From Attendance Crisis to Chronic Condition? Tracking Post-Pandemic Chronic Absenteeism into 2025" (national rate about 28% in 2022, 23.5% in 2024, improvement under one point in 2025; grade-level data showing post-pandemic cohorts equally elevated): https://www.aei.org/research-products/report/from-attendance-crisis-to-chronic-condition-tracking-post-pandemic-chronic-absenteeism-into-2025/ - American Enterprise Institute, October 19, 2026 — "New Hope on Student Absenteeism" (21 states with 2026 data all improved; early-reporter caveat): https://www.aei.org/domestic-policy/education/new-hope-on-student-absenteeism/ - K-12 Dive, July 23, 2026 — NWEA analysis: districts with persistently high chronic absenteeism about 50% further from math recovery; AEI on the goal of cutting 2022 rates in half (18 states adopted): https://www.k12dive.com/news/chronic-absenteeisms-impact-on-academic-recovery/825926/ - FutureEd and Attendance Works, October 2026 — Attendance Playbook, third edition (more than 30 strategies; Mathematica review of 150+ studies; connectedness strongest): https://www.future-ed.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2026AttendancePlaybook.pdf - Education Week, October 2026 — "Want to Improve Attendance? Start With Relationships" (Everyone Graduates Center / Partnership for Student Success principal surveys): https://www.edweek.org/leadership/want-to-improve-attendance-start-with-relationships/2026/10 - National Center for Education Evaluation, REL Appalachia, June 2026 — "Strengthening Attendance Using Multi-Tiered Family Engagement Strategies" (four root-cause categories): https://nces.ed.gov/sites/default/files/rel-appalachia/document/2026/07/RELAP_6-2-21_Chronic-Absenteeism_Infographic_06262026_Acc.pdf - Attendance Works and Johns Hopkins Everyone Graduates Center, June 2, 2026 — school-level chronic absence analysis, 2024-25 data from 31 states (extreme-level schools down from 41% in 2021-22 to 23% in 2024-25): https://www.attendanceworks.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Attendance-Works-JHU-data-blog-PR-final-060126.pdf - Attendance Works, June 2024 — "Stemming the Surge in Chronic Absence: What States Can Do" (state policy review; New Hampshire among the states adopting the 10% definition). Verify: search attendanceworks.org for "Stemming the Surge in Chronic Absence". - Londonderry School District — Superintendent Dan Black, Fall 2026 Superintendent Video Newsletter Part 2, Absences (about 93% daily attendance; goal 97%, six absences or fewer), October 15, 2026, as republished by TownUnderground: https://townunderground.com/?p=13191 - Salem, New Hampshire School Board, January report — Salem High School 981 fewer absence days and about 1,620 fewer tardies in the first 18 weeks year over year; Woodbury School 367 fewer absences; five parent-excused absences per year, then third-party documentation. Verify: search citizenportal.ai for "Salem School officials report fewer absences and tardies after new attendance" and the Salem School District board minutes for January. - Manchester School District, Committee on Student Conduct, February 2025 — truancy communication steps at 5, 10, and 15 unexcused days, DCYF referral at 20, medical-verification practice at about 20 excused absences, pre-K attendance data accuracy warning. Verify: search citizenportal.ai for "Manchester district January attendance dipped amid illnesses". - Manchester School District, October 2025 — fall attendance snapshot (92.3% attending 80-100% of days; goal 95% by June 30) and Project AWARE (five-year, $7.6 million federal grant; 2023 YRBS help-seeking data). Verify: search citizenportal.ai for "Manchester district data most students have zero office referrals" and "Manchester updates Project AWARE". - New Hampshire iNHDEX, 2025-2026 specifications — districts submit excused and unexcused absences and suspensions; data used to calculate chronic absenteeism and attendance rate at district and school level: https://inhdex.getalma.com/public/2025-2026/651c86d3e571430515eaeeae - RSA 189:35-a, Truancy Defined — ten half days of unexcused absence in a school year constitute habitual truancy: https://law.justia.com/codes/new-hampshire/2022/title-xv/title-189/section-189-35-a/ - RSA 189:34 — school board truancy policy duties (definition of excused absence, intervention process, designated employee per school). Verify: search law.justia.com for "New Hampshire Revised Statutes Section 189:34". - RSA 193-E:3 — annual district reporting indicators, including attendance rates, disaggregated by subgroup including pupils with disabilities: https://law.justia.com/codes/new-hampshire/title-xv/chapter-193-e/section-193-e-3/ - HB 1573 (2026), Chapter 307, signed July 10, 2026 — schools must excuse up to two absences per year for civic engagement and career and technical education activities, with parental notice; extended learning opportunity route for ongoing participation: https://Legiscan.com/NH/text/HB1573/2026 - Attendance Works and Healthy Schools Campaign — early-grade chronic absence research (at least 10% of kindergartners and first graders miss a month or more). Verify: search edweek.org for "Early Patterns of Chronic Absenteeism Threaten Academic Success".
